formats.key: Session(address owner,address delegate,uint48 validAfter,uint48 validUntil,uint32 maxCalls,uint16 maxFeeBps,AssetLimit[] limits,bytes32 salt)AssetLimit(address token,uint256 limit)
effects: Anyone holding the signature can call createSessionBySig and register a session in the owner's name for `delegate`, keyed by (owner, delegate, salt).
The delegate can then sign call intents that allowlisted Flying Tulip target contracts execute for the owner, spending the owner's tokens.
Per listed token, spending is capped at `limit` and the cap goes down with each spend; a limit of type(uint256).max is never decremented (unlimited). Tokens not listed cannot be spent.
The session is only usable between validAfter and validUntil; validUntil = 0 means it never expires.
At most maxCalls delegate calls are allowed; maxCalls = 0 means unlimited calls (only allowed when validUntil != 0).
Each call can pay a relayer fee of up to maxFeeBps of the output amount, taken from what the owner receives.
The session stays active until it expires, runs out of calls, or the owner revokes it.
formats.shown: "Create session" / "FT session <delegate>", with owner, delegate, start and end dates, max calls, max fee in bps, and the per-token limit amount (token taken from limits.[].token).

findings.title: Session: validUntil 0 (no expiry) and maxCalls 0 (unlimited) are shown as a 1970 date and '0'.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.sol SessionConfig: `uint48 validUntil; // 0 = no expiry`, `uint32 maxCalls; // 0 = unlimited`; _createSession only rejects both being 0. Descriptor: validUntil uses format date with no special handling; maxCalls uses format raw.
findings.fix: Show 0 as 'Never expires' for validUntil and 'Unlimited' for maxCalls, e.g. with a label or message for 0 if the spec allows it; at least change the labels to say what 0 means.

findings.title: Session intent 'Create session' does not say the delegate gets to spend the signer's tokens.
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent "Create session", interpolatedIntent "FT session {delegate}". Code: validateAndConsume lets allowlisted targets spend the owner's tokens up to tokenAllowance[sessionId][token] on calls the delegate signs.
findings.fix: Use an intent like "Authorize session key" and an interpolatedIntent like "Let {delegate} spend your tokens until {validUntil}".

findings.title: Session: the token of each spending limit is not its own field; an unresolved token shows a bare raw integer.
findings.evidence: Case 0 screen: 'Token limit' = "100000000000000000000" with no token name or address (token 0xF7D8...9C9C on chain 146 was not resolved). Descriptor shows only limits.[].limit with tokenPath limits.[].token.
findings.fix: Add a field for `limits.[].token` (format addressName with types ["token"], or tokenTicker) so the signer can see which token each limit covers even when the wallet does not resolve it.

findings.title: Session: what the delegate can do depends on the allowlisted target set held in storage.
findings.evidence: SessionManager.validateAndConsume: `if (!allowedTarget[msg.sender]) revert TargetNotAllowed(msg.sender);` The allowlist is set by the contract owner (setAllowedTarget) and is not in the message.
findings.fix: No descriptor change; the label or intent can mention 'Flying Tulip contracts'.

findings.title: Session 'Max fee' does not say it is a relayer fee taken from the signer's output on each call.
findings.evidence: SessionConfig `uint16 maxFeeBps; // max relayer fee vs output amount`. Descriptor label "Max fee".
findings.fix: Label it "Max relayer fee per call".

findings.title: The Session test never covers the special values or a token the wallet can resolve.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json uses validUntil 1770600000, maxCalls 100, and token 0xF7D8... that renders raw.
findings.fix: Add cases with validUntil 0, maxCalls 0, a limit of type(uint256).max, and a known token.

couldNotCheck: The allowlisted target contracts that call validateAndConsume (e.g. MintAndRedeem) are not in the directory. They decide which of the owner's tokens move, how much (spendToken/spendAmount), and the fee. So I could not confirm that a session only allows spending within the limits shown.
